topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the opening framing, welcome, and key learning objectives for the lecture on the causes of cancer.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology and the Interplay of Genetics, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental nature of cancer as an evolutionary and genetic disease shaped by endogenous mutations, environmental exposures, and epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Agents in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive malignancy, focusing on oncogenic viruses and the mechanistic case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how dietary toxins, ultraviolet radiation, and chemical carcinogens cause DNA damage directly or via metabolic activation into reactive intermediates.

topics.label: Tumor Promoters, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic factors, including tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and developmental or tissue-specific contexts, drive cancer progression.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Evaluating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogens and determine their potency.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing remarks and summarizing thoughts on weighing environmental risks against daily life benefits.
